extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2026 reviewers (prospective and assigned paper reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewing papers submitted to ICLR 2026, covering reviewer responsibilities, how to read and evaluate submissions, required disclosures, organization of reviews, discussion and final recommendation procedures, and expected timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely and substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your reviews are timely and substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must meet deadlines for writing and updating reviews. Timely, high-quality reviews are essential; late or poor-quality reviews will be subject to penalties (e.g., blocking access to reviews of the reviewer's own submissions during rebuttal, warnings, and possible desk rejection of the reviewer's papers if low-quality reviews are not corrected). Follow specified review windows and AC deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to Code of Ethics (CoE)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers are required to read and adhere to the ICLR Code of Ethics and to raise potential CoE violations as part of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must complete a CoE report when submitting reviews (a two-question form: whether there's a potential violation, and if so explanation). Read the CoE before starting reviews. Authors may include CoE discussions in their papers in a section that does not count toward page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose use of Large Language Models (LLMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must disclose any use of LLMs in their reviews; reviewers take full responsibility for content written under their name (including LLM-generated content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review form includes a field to specify LLM usage. Failing to disclose may risk desk rejection of the reviewer's own papers. Reviewers should notify the area chair if undisclosed significant LLM use in an author's submission is discovered. Authors are also asked to disclose significant LLM use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the paper thoroughly and consult related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read the entire paper and look up related work and citations to comprehensively evaluate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give yourself sufficient time. Supplementary material is not necessary to read but can often answer questions, so consult it before asking authors. Understand the context and prior work to judge motivation and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the paper's objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the objective: address a known application/problem, draw attention to a new problem/application, introduce/explain a new theoretical finding, or a combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objectives imply different criteria for value and impact—tailor your evaluation (e.g., empirical rigor vs theoretical clarity) to the paper's stated goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and list strong and weak points
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the submission's strengths and weaknesses (clarity, technical correctness, experimental rigor, reproducibility, novelty, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as comprehensive as possible. Distinguish between major and minor weaknesses. Use concrete examples from the paper to justify claims about strengths/weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of bias and be open-minded
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid letting personal biases overly influence assessment; consider the paper's value to the broader ICLR community even if not of interest to you personally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to fairly assess contributions across theory, empirics, and practice. Note potential reviewer-specific limitations or unfamiliarity with a subarea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer four key questions to form recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: For accept/reject, address: (1) What specific question/problem is tackled? (2) Is the approach well motivated and well-placed in the literature? (3) Does the paper support its claims (correctness, rigor)? (4) What is the significance of the work (new, relevant, impactful knowledge)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these questions as the core of your decision. Significance does not require state-of-the-art performance; it requires convincing demonstration of new, relevant contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize the initial review clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the review as: summary of claimed contributions; list of strong and weak points; clear initial recommendation (accept/reject) with 1–2 key reasons; supporting arguments; questions for authors; additional constructive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be positive and constructive in the summary. Make clear which feedback is for improving the paper vs. which affects the decision. Ask specific questions that will help you assess the paper during author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete the CoE report when submitting the review
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a review, complete the two-question CoE report (whether there is a potential CoE violation, and an explanation if yes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer should read the Code of Ethics prior to completing this. Indicate potential violations in the CoE report; ACs will work with PCs and the ethics board to resolve cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage actively in discussion and be willing to revise recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in asynchronous discussion with authors, other reviewers, and ACs during the discussion phase and be open to changing your recommendation based on new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with other reviewers' feedback before any borderline meetings. ACs may schedule virtual meetings for borderline papers; reviewers are expected to attend when requested (absence can be noted). Use discussion to clarify and improve assessment; reviewers can change reviews after author response period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a final recommendation with updated reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: After the discussion and any paper revisions, update your review and state your final recommendation, explaining what changed and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how the discussion/author responses affected your view. Update both decision and supporting arguments accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting additional experiments: scope limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may ask for additional experiments, but they should not request experiments that significantly change the paper's content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New experiments should be limited in scope and meant to further validate existing claims rather than alter the paper's main contribution. Ask for experiments that are feasible within the rebuttal period and that directly address key concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOTA not required for acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission not achieving state-of-the-art results is not by itself grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the paper convincingly demonstrates new, relevant, and impactful knowledge. Papers can provide value through theory, empirical insights, methods for practitioners, or other contributions without being strictly SOTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations on citing contemporaneous and arXiv work
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are not required to compare to contemporaneous peer-reviewed work published within two months of the deadline; arXiv is not considered peer-reviewed so comparisons to arXiv-only papers are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If aware of contemporaneous or arXiv works, authors are encouraged to cite them; reviewers may point them out, but lack of such comparisons cannot be a basis for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess theoretical soundness, assumptions, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether theoretical claims are correct, assumptions are stated, proofs are clear, and novelty is properly established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask authors to clarify unclear theorems/assumptions, point out possible gaps in proofs or logical steps, and request precise statements about novelty relative to prior work. Sample reviews illustrate requesting clarifications on theorems, assumptions, and derivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess experimental rigor, reproducibility, and statistical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate experiments for clarity, adequate baselines, hyperparameter tuning, number of runs, statistical significance, computational cost, and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request missing experimental details (e.g., policies used, reward functions, parameter tuning, initialization, number of seeds/runs). Check whether results are significant and whether computational costs or ablation studies are discussed. Use supplementary material before asking for clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback aimed to improve the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond decision-related critiques, give additional feedback to help authors improve clarity, presentation, and technical content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it clear which points are for improvement versus decision-critical. Use respectful tone; include minor comments (typos, unclear phrases) and suggestions for organization and exposition. Sample reviews include 'Things to improve' lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag other policy violations and contact appropriate parties
rubrics_metrics.description: For violations such as plagiarism, double submission, length/formatting issues, contact AC/SAC/PC or use confidential comments with appropriate readership restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Code of Ethics issues use the CoE report. For other policy concerns, send confidential comments to ACs/SACs/PC as appropriate so they can coordinate resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reviewer administrative tasks by stated deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform scheduled reviewer tasks: create/update OpenReview profile, bid on papers, write initial reviews, engage in discussion, flag CoE issues by specified dates, and provide recommendations by deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the timeline provided (profile by Sep 19 2025, bidding Sep 28–Oct 4 2025, initial reviews Oct 10–Nov 01 2025, discussion Nov 11–Dec 3 2025, CoE flagging by Nov 26 2025, recommendations by Dec 03 2025). Meeting attendance for borderline cases may be requested between Dec 03–10.
